name: gh-flow
description: One-shot issue-to-PR compositions: the ordinary chain, a spec-driven autopilot, a backlog drain, dependency waves, and a single-issue descendant wave.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the gh-flow skills.

The authoritative mapping is not in this repo. It lives in the sibling repo `dEitY719/harness-skills` at `references/kimi-tools.md` (https://github.com/dEitY719/harness-skills/blob/main/references/kimi-tools.md) and is the single source of truth for every repo in the `dEitY719/*-skills` family; do not copy it here. Summary:

- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or `"explore"` (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`. `gh-flow:autopilot` delegates implementation this way; the delegating session still verifies the diff and runs the tests itself rather than trusting the worker's report.
- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Every `git` and `gh` call in these skills is a plain shell command - run it with `Bash` and surface its `[OK]` / `[WARN]` / `[FAIL]` lines verbatim.
- `gh` must be installed and authenticated. Each skill binds `TARGET_HOST` and `TARGET_REPO` from the remote URL and prefixes every call with `GH_HOST=` before any API call (dEitY719/dotfiles#1403). Do not drop that prefix; a GHES remote resolves to the wrong server without it.
- Kimi Code has no `Skill` tool, and these five skills are compositions whose whole job is calling other skills. Without it they cannot run as written: print the ordered list of atomic skills the chain would have invoked, run the ones you can as plain shell, and stop at the first step that genuinely needs another skill. Do not inline a reimplementation of an atomic skill.

Safety contracts. These are part of the skills, not advice:

- None of the five merges a pull request by itself. `gh-flow:autopilot` explicitly stops at review; merging is a human decision. Three explicit exceptions, none merging anything itself: `gh-flow:drain --merge` delegates to `gh-pr:merge-train`, and `gh-flow:waves` and `gh-flow:wave` (merging by default) have each worker delegate to `gh-pr:merge` - their approval and label gates still apply, a refusal is reported `[FAIL] not merged`, and `--no-merge` on either merges nothing. `gh-pr:merge-emergency` is never called by any path.
- `gh-flow:waves`: the coordinator never calls `gh-flow:issue` itself (only its workers do), one worker per worktree, merge judged by `mergeCommit.oid` only, live verification serial and only after every merge of the wave.
- `gh-flow:wave`: the same coordinator and merge rules, one issue at a time, and only open issues marked `Spawned-from: #<N>` from its own tree are processed - never another open issue.
- `gh-flow:drain` ends only when open issues AND deferred items are both zero. Anything found during a run and not fixed in it becomes a new issue via `gh-issue:issue-create`; a ledger line or a PR comment does not count, and a failed promotion stops the round rather than being swallowed.
- `gh-flow:issue` stops at the first failing step and reports a resume hint. It never retries a step and never skips one.
- Zero conversational text between the chained skill calls of `gh-flow:issue` and `gh-flow:autopilot`. A self-authored progress report between calls reads as a final answer and ends the run early - this is the failure mode both skills exist to prevent.

interface.shortDescription: Carry a GitHub issue to a reviewed PR in one run
interface.longDescription: gh-flow bundles the five issue-to-PR composition skills: issue, autopilot, drain, waves, and wave.
